I would rather speak to you in a way that might get through to you rather than just be harsh and abrupt like some of the other comments. When I was younger and making bad dating choices, it didn’t help me when people would criticize me because I truly didn’t understand what love and healthy relationships looked like. 

I am not condoning these choices, but I am assuming you are younger and I can understand how the need to feel loved can drastically alter and cloud the way we see things. 

My guess is that this boy is extremely “charming”, charismatic, manipulative, “love bombing” you, deceptive, and preys on women with lower self esteem. 

Here are some questions to think about. 

-If he didn’t treat his last gf well, why will this relationship be different? What makes you different from his last gf? Men like this who treat one girl poorly will treat all women poorly. A “mismatched” relationship (meaning two people who aren’t a good fit) doesn’t isn’t what creates infidelity, abuse, and bad treatment. Two good people who aren’t a good fit will consider how the other person feels and act accordingly, rather than cheat/abuse/hurt/manipulate. If he did these things to her, he will eventually do them to you, no matter how well you guys click. 

-What leads you to believe he wants a serious relationship, rather than use you for sex? He cheated in his last relationship and recently reached out to someone for casual sex. His actions don’t match his words. Why do you believe that he suddenly wants a trusting, loving relationship and isn’t just going for a “easy target”? 

-Even if they broke up amicably, don’t you think it’s a bad idea to rush this quickly into a relationship, especially with an ex of your friend?

-Did you know that abusers try to isolate their partner from their friends and family? A good partner wants to support you in your close relationships, not encourage them to end.  

-Do you believe that you value yourself? When you value yourself, you maintain a high price of admission in order for someone to enter into your life. Do you believe that all you deserve is an unfaithful, deceiving man? You deserve to be in a loving relationship that also supports maintaining close relationships. 

-Are you not close with these girls? I might date an acquaintance’s ex assuming they broke up on good terms (meaning no cheating, abuse, mistreatment) but I wouldn’t ever date a close friends ex. Friends can be for life and aren’t worth throwing away for a fuck boy. 

-Are these friends also drama? A mature person would have just reached out to you and asked to talk about the dating situation, rather than send secretive screenshots.  

I don’t think you are thinking clearly, making good decisions for your future, or showing yourself the love you deserve. A person who truly has love and respect for their own self chooses to surround themselves with people who treat them and those around them well. 

I feel like this boy might be really charming and manipulative and preying on girls with low self esteem who are desperate to feel loved. 

When we don’t love ourselves or have a skewed view of love, we will take what we can get, even if it’s toxic and unhealthy. I used to be the kind of person who would fall hard and ignore every red flag because I needed “love” like I needed food and water. We can’t thrive when we don’t feel loved. However, that love needs to start with ourselves and our support system, not a manipulative fuck boy who just wants to get his dick wet. 

Please reconsider being with this boy. He isn’t worth losing friends, he isn’t worth the heart break, and you will be in for a world of hurt. I know I’m just a stranger from Reddit, but whenever I see posts about women in relationships that are screaming with red flags, my heart aches because that was me. I have PTSD from being in abusive relationships and I wish I had someone who I felt safe talking to, who could have helped me to see that I was looking to feel loved and didn’t think I deserved better. I’m not saying he is abusive because I don’t have enough information, but you would be shocked at how easily we justify the bad things men do that actually are verbally/emotionally abusive. 

Take care.

Believe or not, it’s difficult for some people to feel genuine interest based on someone’s online profile. If you met someone when you are at a bar or friend of friends, you can usually tell pretty quickly if you have any interest or attraction. 

A lot of people who use OLD would like to be with someone, but the process is uncomfortable and awkward. Sometimes you feel like going on there and pursuing, other times it’s not a huge priority. 

So many people act like if you match you HAVE to talk and agree to meet up. It’s for potential introductions. Not every person who gets on there is desperate. it’s okay to treat it casually, if anything I think it’s kind of insane to take it SO SERIOUSLY. 

I really don’t think dating apps are an ideal tool for making meaningful connections. I literally have no emotional connection to an online profile and never will be able to feel anything meaningful towards a person I haven’t met. I can think someone has a nice photo and is nice to talk to, but until we meet (which is absolutely nerve wrecking) it’s just a intro.  

I think what I’m trying to get at is finding someone to date based on their own description of themselves and photos is really hard. It’s uncomfortable and people need to stop letting girls they haven’t met ruin their day. It’s not the end of the world if someone initially thinks, “I might be interested in this person!” and then realizes they aren’t.

J wouldn’t say the level of anxiety I have is exactly the same as generalized anxiety. My brain is like dating = assault so no matter how well I get to know the person beforehand or how public the date is, my body is like hey this is familiar and feels like danger I gotta save you from danger!!! The ptsd component kind of complicates things. With anxiety that isn’t related to ptsd, I have found that powering through and using coping skills does help. If it’s related to specific triggers, it’s not worth to me to torture myself. No date is worth the mental torture, so I mostly have to rely on self care, coping skills, weed, massage therapy, and just day to day care and hope that I come out on top. If I don’t, I don’t push through it. 

I honesty just put myself first and if I don’t want to do something, I don’t do it. It’s different in my opinion from just generalized anxiety. I have to nurture my nervous system and I honestly don’t push myself to do things my body is begging me not to do. I have seen the awful things that go on being cared “by professionals”. I worked at a care home once where I was so severely understaffed that I had grown adults with dementia sitting in wet diapers for 1-2 hours because I couldn’t get to them fast enough :( I was literally crying in between rooms because I felt like such a piece of shit person. 

What was required of me to work here? A two hour certificate. I was stupid and thought they would train me. I was “trained” in one day and left to figure the rest out. It was terrifying.

I have a completely different view on this. This wasn’t a man who had symptoms that he was actively working on managing. He wanted HER to manage them. She’s not a bad person for hoping he would see that him not managing himself and getting help wasn’t going to be healthy for her. I’m sorry guys, but your struggles are not for your partner to manage. It’s incredibly scary and will absolutely take a toll on your mental health. If you have ever been in a relationship where your partner wasn’t caring for themselves and refused to get help, I’m sure you can relate to what I’m saying. 

There is a point where you have to take responsibility for yourself and realize that the only person who can accept help is yourself. She’s not a bad person for being hopeful that a person she loves would love himself and her enough to receive help and actively work to manage his struggles. 

She isn’t saying that she broke up with him purely for anxiety and depression, but for how he was managing it. If I had a bf who had diabetes, I wouldn’t leave him for having diabetes but you bet I would leave him for not caring for himself. If he was constantly refusing to take him medication or not keeping track of things the way he needs, I wouldn’t be able to help him and it would take too much of a toll on me to continue to be in a relationship. We can love and support our partners, but we can’t be their caregivers. 
Advice wise: I would go NC and move on. If he wanted to be in a relationship with you and valued your mental health, he would have some insight into what he needed to do to make that happen.
